question: A chat server stores 40 000 open sockets in an array and, on disconnect, runs `sockets.splice(sockets.indexOf(socket), 1)`. CPU spikes when many users disconnect at once. What is the cheapest correct change?
options: Store the sockets in a `Set` (O(1) delete, insertion order kept), or keep a linked-list node on each socket and remove it in O(1)
Sort the array so `indexOf` is faster
explanation: `indexOf` plus `splice` is O(n) per disconnect. A Set is the least code; a linked list with handles also allows reordering by activity.

question: A hand-written `remove(node)` updates `node.prev.next` and `node.next.prev` when they exist but never touches `head` or `tail`. Which bug appears?
options: Removing the first or last node leaves `head` or `tail` pointing at a removed node, so later pushes or shifts corrupt the list
It throws a TypeError on every call
explanation: Edge nodes have no neighbor on one side; the list's own `head`/`tail` must be updated instead. Pointer bugs are silent, so test head, tail and single-node removals.

question: When is a plain array the better choice over a linked list?
options: When you mostly iterate or access by index and rarely remove from the middle
When you remove nodes by handle thousands of times per second
When you need O(1) insertion at the front
Never: linked lists are always faster
explanation: Arrays are contiguous in memory, which makes iteration and indexed access very fast. Linked lists only win for removal or reordering by reference.
